strings.name: Rafael Grossi
strings.summary: Grossi moved from Argentina’s foreign service into non-proliferation and international organizations, becoming IAEA director general in 2019 and beginning a second term in 2023. He led missions to Ukrainian nuclear facilities and works on Iran safeguards and diplomacy. Results depend on the agency’s mandate and member-state cooperation; disputes are not guaranteed resolution. Argentina nominated him for UN Secretary-General in 2025, which is not appointment.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 13 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Leading the IAEA, he participates in nuclear-facility safety, international verification and diplomacy over regional nuclear issues, influencing global security.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.highlights.h1.title: Wartime nuclear safety
strings.highlights.h1.text: Led the IAEA team to Zaporizhzhya, establishing continued expert presence and safety monitoring.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Education at Argentina’s Catholic University and diplomatic academy; international relations PhD, Geneva Graduate Institute (1997).
strings.highlights.h2.title: Verification and diplomacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Conducts diplomacy on Iran’s nuclear programme and international safeguards, advocating political solutions.
strings.timeline.t1.title: UN Secretary-General nomination
strings.timeline.t1.text: Argentina nominated him; nomination is not presented as appointment at cutoff.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Second term begins
strings.timeline.t2.text: Began a second four-year term with Board and General Conference support.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Zaporizhzhya mission
strings.timeline.t3.text: Led the IAEA mission to the Russian-controlled plant, followed by continued expert presence.
strings.timeline.t4.title: IAEA director general
strings.timeline.t4.text: Became the agency’s sixth director general.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Nuclear Suppliers Group chair
strings.timeline.t5.text: Began two consecutive chairmanships, serving until 2016.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Ambassador to Austria
strings.timeline.t6.text: Also represented Argentina at the IAEA and Vienna-based international organizations.
strings.timeline.t7.title: International relations doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.title: Foreign-service entry
strings.timeline.t8.text: Joined Argentina’s foreign ministry, moving into international security and multilateral affairs.
